where: lesson learn, Sources card (LSRC has no 'learn' entry)
what: The lesson makes specific evidence claims: the Aswan audit with exact percentages, Hatala 2003, the expertise reversal effect, retrieval practice, spacing, combining pattern recognition with analysis, calibration. Its Sources card lists only Berend 2014 (an NEJM review of acid–base physiology), which supports none of them. This breaks the 'cite everything' rule on the page that argues the app is evidence-based.
evidence: Open lesson learn, expand Sources: 'Sources · 1', Berend only. I confirmed the audit numbers match Musa Hussain E et al., Cureus 2024;16(12):e74906, doi:10.7759/cureus.74906 (pH 82.9%, primary disorder 82.1%, compensation 47% → 78.4%, AG 69.2%, HCO₃⁻ link 64.1%, consistency 71.8%).
fix: Add SRC entries and LSRC.learn=['hussain24','hatala03','ark06','kalyuga03','roediger06','cepeda06','meyer13']: Musa Hussain E et al. Cureus 2024;16:e74906; Hatala RM, Brooks LR, Norman GR. Adv Health Sci Educ 2003;8:17–26; Ark TK, Brooks LR, Eva KW. Acad Med 2006;81:405–409; Kalyuga S et al. Educ Psychol 2003;38:23–31; Roediger HL, Karpicke JD. Psychol Sci 2006;17:249–255; Cepeda NJ et al. Psychol Bull 2006;132:354–380; Meyer AND et al. JAMA Intern Med 2013;173:1952–1958. Remove Berend from this lesson (it only comes from MSRC.start), or keep it and add the others.

what: The red-cell lesson (Bohr, Haldane, chloride shift, CO₂ carriage 90/5/5 and 30/10 shares, 2,3-BPG) cites Kraut & Madias 2014 'Lactic acidosis', Rose & Post, and Severinghaus 1966 'Blood gas calculator'. None of them is a source for red-cell CO₂ transport. The micro module default (kraut14) puts the lactic acidosis paper on every micro lesson, including acidsrc, rbc and toxalc, where it supports nothing.
fix: Set MSRC.micro=['rose'] and add kraut14 only to lactate/microbes (it is already in LSRC.lactate). Add 'west' and 'nunn' to LSRC.rbc (West's Respiratory Physiology ch. 6 gives the 90/5/5 and exchanged-CO₂ shares).

what: uosm cites Purssell 2001, which is about ethanol's contribution to the PLASMA osmolal gap, not the urine osmolal gap. The urine osmolal gap thresholds (<150, NH₄⁺ ≈ gap ÷ 2) are unsourced.
evidence: c5.js line 75: uosm:['batlle88','purssell01']; SRC.purssell01 = Ann Emerg Med 2001;38:653 'contribution of ethanol to the osmolal gap'.
fix: Replace purssell01 with Kim GH, Han JS, Kim YS, Joo KW, Kim S, Lee JS. Evaluation of urine acidification by urine anion gap and urine osmolal gap in chronic metabolic acidosis. Am J Kidney Dis 1996;27:42–47 (PMID 8546137); optionally add Kraut JA, Madias NE. Differential diagnosis of nongap metabolic acidosis. Clin J Am Soc Nephrol 2012;7:671–679.

what: traps is cited only to AARC 2013 and Toffaletti 2007, neither of which covers the low anion gap, IgG paraprotein, bromide/lithium or albumin correction that make up most of the lesson.
evidence: c5.js line 76: traps:['aarc13','toff07']. kraut07 (Kraut & Madias 2007 CJASN 2:162, 'Serum anion gap: its uses and limitations') is already in SRC.
fix: traps:['kraut07','aarc13','toff07'] and also add kraut07 to analyser (pseudohyponatraemia/total CO₂).

what: Lesson text quotes EXTRIP 2015 thresholds but the only lesson source is Kraut & Madias 2010; EXTRIP is not in SRC. Breaks the 'cite everything' rule for dialysis criteria.
fix: Add SRC extrip15asa: 'Juurlink DN, et al. Extracorporeal treatment for salicylate poisoning: systematic review and recommendations from the EXTRIP workgroup. Ann Emerg Med 2015;66:165–181.' and Proudfoot AT, Krenzelok EP, Vale JA. Position paper on urine alkalinization. J Toxicol Clin Toxicol 2004;42:1–26 (urine pH 7.5–8.5); add both to LSRC.asa.

what: Table is labelled 'BTS/SIGN 2019' but BTS/SIGN is not among the sources (only Epstein 2001, Foster 2001 + module defaults).
fix: Add SRC sign158: 'British Thoracic Society/SIGN. SIGN 158 British guideline on the management of asthma. 2019.' to LSRC.asthma (and Rodrigo 2004 or similar for salbutamol lactate if wanted).

what: Body heading says 'Diagnosis (2024 international consensus)' but that consensus is not cited; listed sources are JBDS 2023 plus two paediatric papers.
fix: Add SRC ada24: 'Umpierrez GE, et al. Hyperglycemic crises in adults with diabetes: a consensus report. Diabetes Care 2024;47:1257–1275.' to LSRC.dka.

what: PE lesson cites only Foster 2001 (respiratory alkalosis). The '≈ one fifth have a normal A–a gradient' claim and the diagnostic advice (clinical probability, D-dimer, imaging) have no source.
fix: Add Konstantinides SV, et al. 2019 ESC Guidelines for acute pulmonary embolism. Eur Heart J 2020;41:543–603, and Stein PD, et al. Arterial blood gas analysis in the assessment of suspected acute pulmonary embolism. Chest 1996;109:78–81, to LSRC.pe.

what: Post-ROSC targets (PaCO2 35–45, SpO2 94–98%, ETCO2 < 10 mmHg at 20 min, bicarbonate only for hyperkalaemia/TCA) come from ERC/ESICM guidance but the only lesson-specific source is Kraut & Madias 2014 (lactic acidosis). 'Cite everything' roadmap rule broken for the core numbers.
evidence: Sources panel on arrest shows Berend 2014, Kraut 2010, Kraut 2014 only (run: openLesson('arrest'), expand Sources).
fix: Add to SRC: nolan21: 'Nolan JP, Sandroni C, Böttiger BW, et al. European Resuscitation Council and European Society of Intensive Care Medicine guidelines 2021: post-resuscitation care. Resuscitation 2021;161:220–269.' and soar21: 'Soar J, et al. ERC Guidelines 2021: Adult advanced life support. Resuscitation 2021;161:115–151.' Set LSRC.arrest=['nolan21','soar21','kraut14'].

what: Heat stroke definition, cooling priority and gas evolution are sourced only to Foster 2001 (respiratory alkalosis). No heat-illness source at all.
evidence: Sources panel on heat: Berend, Kraut 2010, Foster 2001.
fix: Add: 'Epstein Y, Yanovich R. Heatstroke. N Engl J Med 2019;380:2449–2459.' and 'Bouchama A, et al. Classic and exertional heatstroke. Nat Rev Dis Primers 2022;8:8.' and 'Roberts WO, et al. ACSM expert consensus statement on exertional heat illness. Curr Sports Med Rep 2023;22:134–149.' LSRC.heat=[those, 'foster01'].

what: The kidney model is placed in 'Why metabolic alkalosis persists' (alkmaint), but it has no alkalosis content: no volume or chloride depletion, no hypokalaemia, no pendrin/β-intercalated cell, no paradoxical aciduria. All its toggles are acidosis states. The learner gets a model unrelated to the lesson's message.
evidence: openLesson('alkmaint') → the model 'Kidney: reclaiming and making bicarbonate' with Acid load / Acetazolamide / Type 1 / Type 4 only. The lesson text covers maintenance by volume, Cl⁻, K⁺ and aldosterone.
fix: Remove 'kidney' from alkmaint in c9.js until the model has an alkalosis mode. Or (e3.js) add a 'Vomiting: low Cl⁻ and volume' toggle: proximal reclaim ↑ (Na⁺ avidity), β-cell pendrin cannot secrete HCO₃⁻ without luminal Cl⁻, H⁺ secretion ↑ with hypokalaemia/aldosterone, urine pH acid (paradoxical aciduria), urine Cl⁻ < 20.

what: Asthma sim cites davidson16 (BTS/ICS guideline on ventilation for acute HYPERCAPNIC respiratory failure, which does not cover acute asthma) and BTS oxygen 2017; there is no acute asthma guideline in the registry at all.
evidence: grep c5.js: no SIGN/BTS asthma key; sim-asthma src:['davidson16','odriscoll17'].
fix: Add bts19:['BTS/SIGN 158','British Thoracic Society/Scottish Intercollegiate Guidelines Network. British guideline on the management of asthma (SIGN 158), 2019 (acute asthma section retained in BTS/NICE/SIGN 2024).'] to SRC and use src:['bts19','odriscoll17'] in c12.js sim-asthma.

what: D-lactic acidosis, secretory diarrhoea and ureterosigmoidostomy claims have no supporting source; only Hess 1979 (pseudohypoxaemia) is lesson-specific.
fix: Add a D-lactate source (Kowlgi 2015 or Uribarri J et al. Medicine 1998;77:73–82) and kraut10 (already in SRC) for diarrhoea/NAGMA.

what: The 2023 global ARDS definition (S/F ≤ 315 with SpO₂ ≤ 97%, HFNO ≥ 30 L/min) is taught and tested (q5) but only Berlin 2012 is cited.
fix: Add SRC.matthay24: 'Matthay MA, et al. A new global definition of acute respiratory distress syndrome. Am J Respir Crit Care Med 2024;209:37–47.' and add to LSRC.ratios. Say 'global definition (2023, published 2024)'.

what: odc and co2vent give SpO₂ targets (BTS) and ventchg teaches permissive hypercapnia and 6 mL/kg PBW without those guidelines in their sources.
evidence: Sources lists: odc = West, Nunn, Severinghaus; co2vent/ventchg = West, Nunn, Epstein.
fix: Add odriscoll17 to odc and co2vent; add fan17 (ATS/ESICM/SCCM 2017) and brackett65 (acute CO₂ titration slope) to ventchg.

what: kacid teaches DKA potassium thresholds but cites only Aronson & Giebisch (and module refs).
fix: kacid:['aronson11','jbds23'].

what: The kidney model embedded in renal credits 'Batlle 1988' but the lesson's Sources list shows only Rose & Post and Soriano (2 sources).
evidence: openLesson('renal') → Sources · 2; model footer 'Sources: Rose & Post; Soriano 2002; Batlle 1988'.
fix: Add batlle88 to LSRC.renal, or have lessonSources merge sources of embedded models.

what: racid cites epstein01 and brackett65 only; its NIV and intubation criteria have no guideline source although davidson16 (BTS/ICS 2016) is in SRC.
fix: racid:['epstein01','brackett65','davidson16'].

what: GOLDMARK (Mehta AN et al. Lancet 2008;372:892) and the EXTRIP metformin recommendation (Calello DP et al. Crit Care Med 2015;43:1716) are taught but not cited. 'Cite everything' is a roadmap decision.
fix: Add SRC.mehta08 and SRC.calello15 and include them in LSRC.hagma.

what: npo2 teaches oxygen targets (94-98%) and FiO2 by device with no source (module default only siggaard74 and aarc13). nlac teaches the Sepsis-3 septic shock definition with only kraut14.
fix: LSRC.npo2:['odriscoll17']; LSRC.nlac:['kraut14','evans21'] plus Singer M et al. JAMA 2016;315:801 (Sepsis-3) as a new SRC entry.

what: Uncited claims: Sepsis-3 definition (Singer 2016 not in SRC); CKD bicarbonate threshold (KDIGO not cited); toxic alcohol dialysis (EXTRIP not cited).
fix: Add Singer M, et al. JAMA 2016;315:801–810 to sepsis; KDIGO 2024 CKD guideline (Kidney Int 2024;105(4S):S117–S314) to renalfail; EXTRIP methanol 2015 and EG 2023 to toxalc2.

what: Two of three DKA-specific sources are paediatric (PECARN FLUID 2018, Glaser 2001) yet the lesson has no paediatric content (no cerebral oedema, no paediatric fluid rates).
fix: Either add a 'Children' bullet (cerebral oedema risk with low PCO₂ and high urea at presentation, Glaser 2001; fluid rate did not change cerebral injury, PECARN 2018; ISPAD 2022) or move these refs to the kids lesson.

what: No source for alcoholic ketoacidosis itself; listed sources are toxic alcohols and lactic acidosis.
fix: Add 'McGuire LC, Cruickshank AM, Munro PT. Alcoholic ketoacidosis. Emerg Med J 2006;23:417–420.' plus NICE CG32 and Purssell 2001.

what: Altitude half of the lesson (Riyadh, Abha values, acetazolamide) has no source.
evidence: Sources panel on preg shows Hegewald only.
fix: Add e.g. 'Luks AM, Swenson ER, Bärtsch P. Acute high-altitude sickness. Eur Respir Rev 2017;26:160096.' and a reference for blood gases at moderate altitude (e.g. Crapo RO et al. Am J Respir Crit Care Med 1999;160:1525, arterial gases at 1,400 m).

what: Massive-transfusion chemistry (citrate, iCa, potassium) and the trauma TXA ≤ 3 h statement have no source; only Kraut 2014 and HALT-IT.
fix: Add 'CRASH-2 collaborators. Lancet 2010;376:23–32 / 2011;377:1096–1101 (TXA ≤ 3 h)' and 'Rossaint R, et al. The European guideline on management of major bleeding and coagulopathy following trauma: sixth edition. Crit Care 2023;27:80' (iCa monitoring and replacement).

where: lesson widget map add{} for icu-ards / icu-obst
what: The ventilator lab embedded in icu-ards and icu-obst opens on "Normal lungs", so the learner has to find the right preset themselves.
evidence: openLesson('icu-ards'): the embedded lab shows Normal lungs, pH 7.49. Screenshot: /tmp/claude-0/-home-claude/80312b5f-0e45-5589-b131-fcf824f33899/scratchpad/beta/shots/T08-icu-ards-desk.png.
fix: Let W.vent.build accept an initial patient (for example add map entries ['vent', {pat:'ards'}] and ['vent', {pat:'asthma'}]), and click that preset on build.

what: No capnography or cyanide source exists in SRC. im-capno cites 'apls' (paediatric life support) and 'west' (respiratory physiology), neither covers waveform capnography; im-dip cites only kraut10 although bosch09 (rhabdomyolysis, NEJM 2009) is already in the registry.
fix: Add: kodali13 (Kodali BS. Capnography outside the operating rooms. Anesthesiology 2013;118:192–201), nap4 (Cook TM et al. NAP4, Br J Anaesth 2011;106:617–631), baud91. Then set im-capno src ['kodali13','nap4'], im-dip src ['bosch09','kraut10'], im-co add 'baud91' (c12.js).

what: The albumin and phosphate charge formulas (0.123·pH − 0.631; 0.309·pH − 0.469) and the SIG come from Figge–Fencl and Kellum. The cited Figge 1998 paper is about anion-gap correction for albumin only.
evidence: Sources card on stewartx: Siggaard-Andersen, Rose, Stewart 1983, Figge 1998.
fix: Add Figge J, Mydosh T, Fencl V. Serum proteins and acid-base equilibria: a follow-up. J Lab Clin Med 1992;120:713–719, and Kellum JA, Kramer DJ, Pinsky MR. Strong ion gap: a methodology for exploring unexplained anions. J Crit Care 1995;10:51–55.

where: LSRC for ph, buffer, ca, dalton, henry
what: These five lessons have only the module textbooks as sources. Specific numbers (Riyadh and Abha barometric pressures, cabin altitude 2,400 m, hyperbaric dissolved O₂ about 6 mL/dL) have no specific support. The numbers are correct by my check (standard atmosphere: 610 m → 707 mmHg, 2,270 m → 577 mmHg; 3 ATA on 100% O₂ → about 6.6 mL/dL).
evidence: Expand the Sources card on each lesson.
fix: Add, for example: dalton → BTS 2011 or Aerospace Medical Association guidance on cabin altitude (≤ 8,000 ft); henry → Undersea and Hyperbaric Medical Society or Boerema 1960 'Life without blood'.

what: The reference card cites wrenn90 (delta gap paper), which has no bearing on normal ranges.
fix: Replace wrenn90 with aarc13 or a laboratory reference source.

what: Every clinical lesson inherits Kraut 2010 (metabolic acidosis) and Berend 2014, so CO, MetHb, opioid and pregnancy lessons show 'Metabolic acidosis: pathophysiology…' as a source for content it does not support.
evidence: Sources panels on methb, preg, opioid.
fix: Make MSRC.clin = ['berend14'] only and add kraut10 to LSRC for the lessons that need it.

what: Sources are plain text, with no DOI or PubMed link and no mapping from claim to source.
fix: Add a DOI/PMID field to SRC and render it as a link (it still works offline as text). Optionally add superscript numbers in the body that point to the list.

what: Sources have no DOI/URL.
fix: Add DOI links so the learner can open the guideline offline-cached or online.
